To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The hard-thermal-loop resummed thermodynamic functions of the gluon plasma have the right sign and magnitude to account for the deviations from lattice gauge theory results for T> 2T{sub {ital c}} and (2) the thermodynamic functions are well described by a quasiparticle model with a temperature dependent mass parameter.

the thermodynamic functions calculated in the HTL approximation are in good agreement with the lattice results, and that the HTL parameters that give the best fit to the thermodynamic functions are in good agreement, within their uncertainties, with the values obtained from other physical quantities.

the HTL thermodynamics of a quark-gluon plasma is well described by the lattice QCD thermodynamics, and that the HTL quasiparticle model can be used to obtain a good approximation of the thermodynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamic functions and the transport coefficients of hot QCD.
the study of the properties of the QCD plasma at high temperature.
the study of thermodynamics of a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in the framework of hard-thermal-loop perturbation theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HTL resummed thermodynamic functions of the hot gluon gas are in good agreement with lattice gauge theory results for T> 2T{sub 1} {sub c}, but are not in good agreement with the lattice data for 1.2T{sub {sub 1}c} < T < 2T{sup c} for any reasonable choice of the HTL parameter.

the HTL perturbation approach is a promising tool to describe the thermodynamics of the QCD plasma at temperatures of the order of 3T{sub c}, and that the HTL thermodynamic potential is in good agreement with lattice calculations.
the HTL thermodynamic quantities are in good agreement with those from lattice calculations and from quark-meson models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HTL perturbation is a good theory for a gluon plasma.
we are able to calculate the thermodynamic properties of a hot gluonic plasma to leading order (LO) in HTL perturbative theory.
we calculated the pressure, energy density, entropy density and the speed of sound of a hot gluonic plasma to leading order of the hard thermal loop (HTL) expansion in the weak-coupling limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HTL thermodynamic potential is in reasonable agreement with the lattice result for T>2 TeV.

the HTL resummation of gluon thermodynamics can be used to estimate the magnitude of next-to-leading order effects in HTL perturbative calculations of gluon thermodynamic functions and transport coefficients.
HTL perturbation is a good starting point for describing the thermodynamics of the gluon plasma.
